<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916037_theRebbe_540" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916037_theRebbe_540__p005">
  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Daas brings resolution to choose good, transcending the indecision of intellect alone, as it draws from Kesser.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And the main aspect of daas is that through it, a decision about a matter is reached.</t>
    <t s="2">That is,</t>
    <t s="3">the discernment between good and evil,</t>
    <t s="4">“the wise discern between good and bad,”</t>
    <t s="5">can also be from the side of Chochmah and Binah,</t>
    <t s="6">but nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="7">he will not have a decision about what to do,</t>
    <t s="8">for from the side of intellect there can be rationales for this and for that.</t>
    <t s="9">And as is known,</t>
    <t s="10">the proof from the generation of the Flood,</t>
    <t s="11">that from that same rationale that necessitated there be a flood,</t>
    <t s="12">“for the inclination of man’s heart is evil from his youth,”</t>
    <t s="13">afterward the conclusion was “I will not again continue to smite,” etc.,</t>
    <t s="14">“and there will no longer be a flood to destroy the earth.”</t>
    <t s="15">That is,</t>
    <t s="16">that from intellect itself one cannot come to a decision,</t>
    <t s="17">and only through daas, which enters into the depth of the matter,</t>
    <t s="18">can one then come to a decision about how to act.</t>
    <t s="19">And this is what is written,</t>
    <t s="20">“and you shall choose life,”</t>
    <t s="21">that is,</t>
    <t s="22">that even though it is already stated,</t>
    <t s="23">“See, I have placed before you… life and good and the opposite,”</t>
    <t s="24">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="25">it is not satisfied with this,</t>
    <t s="26">and it says “and you shall choose life,”</t>
    <t s="27">and particularly according to what the Alter Rebbe said,</t>
    <t s="28">that the letters of “and you shall choose life” are a granting of power that the choice for life can be made,</t>
    <t s="29">from which it is understood that it is not sufficient that one knows that there is life and its opposite,</t>
    <t s="30">because from this very fact it could be that he will choose the opposite, G-d forbid,</t>
    <t s="31">therefore the command “and you shall choose life” is necessary,</t>
    <t s="32">and this is through the aspect of daas, as above.</t>
    <t s="33">But still, it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="34">how is it that through daas one can choose the good,</t>
    <t s="35">for since from the side of intellect,</t>
    <t s="36">even though “the wise discern between good and bad,”</t>
    <t s="37">nevertheless it could be that despite this he will choose the opposite,</t>
    <t s="38">and as it is written,</t>
    <t s="39">“they are wise to do evil,”</t>
    <t s="40">if so,</t>
    <t s="41">how will “and you shall choose life” come about through daas?</t>
    <t s="42">And the explanation of this is,</t>
    <t s="43">that daas connects Chochmah and Binah,</t>
    <t s="44">and thus daas itself is above Chochmah and Binah,</t>
    <t s="45">that is,</t>
    <t s="46">that daas receives from the aspect of Kesser,</t>
    <t s="47">as is known that in a place where daas is counted, Kesser is not counted,</t>
    <t s="48">that is,</t>
    <t s="49">that daas is in the place of Kesser,</t>
    <t s="50">and therefore from this aspect it is possible to have “and you shall choose life.”</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The ultimate knowledge of not knowing is a self-recognition of the soul in Atzmus Ein Sof, enabling the choice of good even for simple Jews.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">9)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation of the matter is,</t>
    <t s="2">that it is known that “the ultimate knowledge is that we do not know,”</t>
    <t s="3">and the simple explanation of this is,</t>
    <t s="4">that first one must understand all that is possible, and afterward one comes to the ultimate knowledge,</t>
    <t s="5">that one understands that in truth one does not know, etc.</t>
    <t s="6">But the inner explanation of this is,</t>
    <t s="7">that the ultimate knowledge is that the knowledge should be in that which we do not know,</t>
    <t s="8">that is,</t>
    <t s="9">that even the aspect of “we do not know” should be in the category of knowledge.</t>
    <t s="10">And the explanation of this is,</t>
    <t s="11">that,</t>
    <t s="12">there is knowledge of affirmation and knowledge of negation.</t>
    <t s="13">Knowledge of affirmation is in Binah,</t>
    <t s="14">which comes in a manner of comprehension,</t>
    <t s="15">that one grasps the intellect through perception and enclothing in seven aspects, etc.</t>
    <t s="16">And knowledge of negation is in Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="17">that is, one understands the intellect by negating from it the matters that oppose and contradict it.</t>
    <t s="18">Nevertheless, it is understood,</t>
    <t s="19">that even the thing grasped through knowledge of negation has a connection to the matters from which it is negated,</t>
    <t s="20">for they are at least within its category,</t>
    <t s="21">and therefore it is possible to negate it from them.</t>
    <t s="22">But there is another aspect of knowledge that does not come even through negation,</t>
    <t s="23">because the matter is not within the category of knowledge at all, such that we could grasp it through negation,</t>
    <t s="24">and this is the aspect of “we do not know.”</t>
    <t s="25">And the explanation of this in the comprehension of G-dliness is,</t>
    <t s="26">that,</t>
    <t s="27">there is the aspect of Memaleh Kol Almin and the aspect of Sovev Kol Almin,</t>
    <t s="28">the aspect of Memaleh Kol Almin is subject to knowledge of affirmation,</t>
    <t s="29">but regarding the aspect of Sovev Kol Almin, only knowledge of negation applies,</t>
    <t s="30">but nevertheless, this is within the category of worlds,</t>
    <t s="31">for it is called Sovev Kol Almin.</t>
    <t s="32">But there is an aspect that is above Sovev Kol Almin,</t>
    <t s="33">even above the general Sovev,</t>
    <t s="34">and even above the true essence of the aspect of Sovev,</t>
    <t s="35">where even knowledge of negation does not apply.</t>
    <t s="36">And it is like what is written in Shaar HaYichud VeHaEmunah,</t>
    <t s="37">that this is like one who says about some lofty and deep wisdom that it is impossible to touch it with hands because of the depth of the concept,</t>
    <t s="38">anyone who hears would laugh at him,</t>
    <t s="39">because the matter of wisdom is not within the category of touch at all,</t>
    <t s="40">even not in a way of negation.</t>
    <t s="41">And about this it is said, “the ultimate knowledge is that we do not know,”</t>
    <t s="42">that even in the aspect of “we do not know” there must be the matter of knowledge,</t>
    <t s="43">and it is that the essence of the soul recognizes the essence of Ein Sof</t>
    <t s="44">(essence grasps essence).</t>
    <t s="45">And like the analogy,</t>
    <t s="46">a small infant who still has smallness of daas or has no daas at all,</t>
    <t s="47">and nevertheless is drawn to his father,</t>
    <t s="48">this is not because of some rationale that he understands how he is his father, etc.,</t>
    <t s="49">but it is only an innate recognition, because he was born from him.</t>
    <t s="50">And this matter is drawn down also into the revealed faculties,</t>
    <t s="51">and it is the aspect of Daas Eloki, which is above Chochmah and Binah,</t>
    <t s="52">and from the side of Daas Eloki there can be the decision to choose good,</t>
    <t s="53">even though from the side of intellect it can be in a manner of “they are wise to do evil.”</t>
    <t s="54">And since the command “and you shall choose life” is for every single Jew,</t>
    <t s="55">it is understood that the power for this is given to every single Jew,</t>
    <t s="56">even to simple people who have no understanding or comprehension,</t>
    <t s="57">that is,</t>
    <t s="58">that the Daas Eloki from the side of the essence is drawn down to the lowest levels to every single Jew,</t>
    <t s="59">even to simple people,</t>
    <t s="60">that they too have the granting of power that there should be “and you shall choose life.”</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The inner aspect of daas enables separation of good and evil through self-recognition of Atzmus, while the eighth king Hadar, the foundation, is the source of rectification through avodah from below to above.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">And all this is from the side of the inwardness of daas,</t>
    <t s="2">but from the side of the externality of daas there can be a mixture of good and evil,</t>
    <t s="3">and this is that the beginning of the shattering was in the aspect of daas,</t>
    <t s="4">for all the cause of the intermingling of good and evil is from the side of daas,</t>
    <t s="5">as above.</t>
    <t s="6">However,</t>
    <t s="7">also the matter of separation between good and evil and the refinement, where one chooses the good and separates the evil, is through daas,</t>
    <t s="8">except that this is from the supernal aspect of daas,</t>
    <t s="9">which is the matter of the innate recognition in the Essence of the Ein Sof light,</t>
    <t s="10">and this aspect and level is only in holiness.</t>
    <t s="11">And this is the matter of the eighth king,</t>
    <t s="12">Hadar,</t>
    <t s="13">about whom it is not said “and he died,”</t>
    <t s="14">because there was no aspect of shattering in him,</t>
    <t s="15">and he is the root and source of rectification.</t>
    <t s="16">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="17">that the eighth king is Yesod,</t>
    <t s="18">and Yesod is the middle line that is drawn from daas,</t>
    <t s="19">and as the saying, “there is no hardness except from daas,”</t>
    <t s="20">and on a higher level,</t>
    <t s="21">it draws from the aspect of Kesser,</t>
    <t s="22">for Kesser is drawn down to the end of the line,</t>
    <t s="23">and therefore we see that in the influence of the drop, the essence is drawn more than in the influence of daas and intellect,</t>
    <t s="24">and as explained from the proof that a blind person gives birth to a complete child, etc.</t>
    <t s="25">And because of this, “and he died” is not said about Hadar,</t>
    <t s="26">because in Yesod there was no aspect of shattering,</t>
    <t s="27">and on the contrary, it is the root and source of rectification,</t>
    <t s="28">which is the matter of refinement.</t>
    <t s="29">And in more detail,</t>
    <t s="30">in the matter of refinement itself there are two modes,</t>
    <t s="31">refinement from above to below,</t>
    <t s="32">and refinement from below to above.</t>
    <t s="33">And,</t>
    <t s="34">when the refinement is in a way of revelation of light from above,</t>
    <t s="35">it can be that sparks of holiness that were extinguished will be pushed away and not be refined,</t>
    <t s="36">and furthermore,</t>
    <t s="37">since the refinement is not from the power of the lower one,</t>
    <t s="38">it can be that after the light departs, the lower one will remain in his level and not be refined.</t>
    <t s="39">Therefore, the refinement must be in a way of avodah from below to above.</t>
    <t s="40">And this is that Yitzchak wanted to bless Esav,</t>
    <t s="41">that is, he wanted to draw upon him a supernal light, through which he would be refined in a passive manner,</t>
    <t s="42">and he erred in this,</t>
    <t s="43">for he would have been completely nullified,</t>
    <t s="44">and his rectification needed to be through Yaakov,</t>
    <t s="45">for then it is in a way of refinement.</t>
    <t s="46">And even though regarding Yaakov it is written “and he gave,” etc.,</t>
    <t s="47">“he gave and again gave,”</t>
    <t s="48">the intention is not that the refinement is through a revelation of light from above,</t>
    <t s="49">but rather this was only in a way of granting power,</t>
    <t s="50">and afterward the refinement must be in a way of avodah from below to above.</t>
    <t s="51">And this matter is accomplished specifically through daas.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
